label: Translated The Tale of Genji into modern Japanese and reclaimed female aesthetics
description: Akiko Yosano's 1912 modern Japanese translation of Murasaki Shikibu's Tale of Genji democratized Heian aesthetics and centered women's subjective emotional and philosophical agency.
dialecticalTension: Bridges classical courtly mono no aware with modern Taishō feminist individualism.
historicalContext: First modern translation of Genji Monogatari (1912–1913).

citations.author: G. G. Rowley
citations.work: Yosano Akiko and The Tale of Genji

label: Debated economic autonomy vs. state motherhood protection (Bosei Hogo Ronsō)
description: In the historic 1918–1919 Motherhood Protection Debate, Akiko Yosano and Raichō Hiratsuka clashed over whether state subsidies for mothers protect women or deepen patriarchal state dependency.
dialecticalTension: Pits liberal-individualist economic self-reliance against social-democratic reproductive justice.
historicalContext: Published across Fujin Kōron and Taiyō in Taishō Japan (1918–1919).

citations.author: Vera Mackie
citations.work: Feminism in Modern Japan: Citizenship, Embodiment and Sexuality
